questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to go on an exchange. I went to Vancouver a few years ago and fell in love with the city, so when I had the opportunity to study and live on Vancouver island so close to the nature and the surroundings I knew I had to go.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: University of Victoria was great about introducing all of the exchange students and we were given a lot of information and help if needed in the first couple days.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any. I found the most difficult thing to be the pre requisite applications for applying for different courses as they were often denied on small things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was through a friend of my family who had gone the university 10 years ago that recommended where I stayed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: This semester when I went to UVIc, no-one got on campus housing if they were an exchange student. Or none that I know of. We heard that they had chosen to prioritize Canadian and first year students. So people applying should be aware of this and look into off campus housing as that may be necessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Difficult. I kept being denied courses I had all the right qualifications for, but obviously had not taken the prerequisite UVic course. This resulted in a lot of email back and forth of me having to convince them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Almost all courses have prerequisites (at least the science ones I had).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails to the exchange team at UVic.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look into all the prerequisites and be prepared to argue that you do have the right qualifications lining up with these.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They were not too challenging. Which I was okay with as I not only wanted to try something new academically during the exchange, but also wanted to focus on the social aspects of it.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were maybe comparative to first or second year courses at KU. (I took third and fourth year UVic courses)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Almost all the focus was on the lectures. Not a lot of reading material prior to lectures, if any. And they focused a lot on attendance. As in it would be difficult to pass the class if not show up, as most of the material would be the lecture slide and information said in class. Even to a point where one of the lectures would leave out words on the slide so you would only get the information if you showed up to class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MICR303 - Immunology 
BIOL459 - Human microbial diseases 
BIOL465 - The Molecular basis of cancer 
ANTH358 - Biology of human skeletal variability

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Human microbial diseases was a super interesting course, but the professor was a bit confusing and the slides very overwhelming. But if you are able to overlook this, the professor is super motivated to teach this information.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The cost of food. The food prices in Canada are extremely high at the moment.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different options.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really participate in any non-academic activities the university did. I went to a few smaller events they planned, but did not participate in any clubs or such.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking and enjoying the nature. UVic is the perfect place to go if you love nature and the outdoors, just a short walk from the beach and beautiful scenery.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, Canadians are super friendly and are happy to include you in stuff.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the local pubs. I met one of my best friends from the exchange just a random night at the pub. He's Canadian and then showed us all the hidden local spots and hikes. Just be open when meeting new people, Canadians are the friendliest people ever!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendliness of Canadian people. Always happy to help and be there if you need anything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be open the first couple of introduction days, join everything you have the energy for. The people you bond with these days are likely to be your friends the rest of the exchange. 
2) Enjoy the nature, get to know someone with a car and go see stuff beyond Victoria on the island. 
3) Be prepared for the course selection, make sure you can argue that you have qualifications for the courses you want.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy it and take every opportunity that comes your way.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made. And getting to go outside of my comfort zone being entirely on my own like this for the first time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to get through everything on my own, challenging and rewarding.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
